# OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Training

> 2-hour online course on OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) and the Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act, for anyone with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials (OPIM). Offered by HAZWOPER OSHA Training (https://hazwoper-osha.com).

## Key facts
- Regulation: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030
- Frequency: required annually for employees with occupational exposure to blood or OPIM
- Duration: about 2 hours; 5 lessons plus final exam
- Credits: 0.2 CEU
- Price: $39.99 per person online; bulk pricing from 2 seats
- Other formats: SCORM, virtual instructor-led, in-person
- Delivery: 100% online, 24/7, any device, full audio read-aloud; English and Spanish
- Completion window: 3 months; 1 year of access to materials
- Certificate: instant PDF on passing, valid 12 months
- Prerequisites: none

## Definitions
- Bloodborne pathogens: infectious microorganisms in human blood that cause disease, including hepatitis B (HBV), hepatitis C (HCV) and HIV.
- Needlestick Safety and Prevention Act (2000): requires safer medical devices, a sharps injury log, and frontline worker input on controls.

## Who it is for
Healthcare workers and first responders; housekeeping, janitorial and laundry staff; laboratory workers and students; tattoo, piercing, cosmetology, construction, maintenance and utility workers; volunteers, community care, education and childcare staff.

## Lessons
1. Introduction to Bloodborne Pathogens
2. Bloodborne Infectious Diseases
3. Exposure Control Plan
4. Vaccination and Post-Exposure Follow-up
5. Emergency Response and Training
